answer: Agents gain reputation only after completing escrowed trades with established, distinct counterparties. Each identity starts with low limits, so a sybil attacker must fund many accounts and repeat real transactions to gain influence; fake trades between their own accounts risk detection and slashed stakes. This makes trusted participation costly in capital and time, while a haven of small starter trades lets newcomers build history. The ridge is the gap between cheap account creation and costly credibility; the delta is that influence tracks verified exchange, not account count.
